method_descriptions.flat: This county's own simple average arrest count over the 4 weeks immediately before this one (not including it). Reacts quickly to a sustained shift, but a single unusual week sits right at the edge of its own baseline and can tilt it.
method_descriptions.guard1: The same 4-week average, but shifted back one extra week: weeks further back than that, skipping the 1 week immediately before this one. The gap ("guard") keeps a recent spike from bleeding into its own comparison point.
method_descriptions.ewma: An exponentially weighted average (α=0.1) built from this county's ENTIRE history up to (not including) this week -- every prior week counts, more recent ones more heavily, with roughly a 9-week effective memory. Smoother than either flat method, since it has no hard window edge, but carries distant history forward longer.

methodology_note: Each week, each county is compared to a baseline built from its own past -- not a population figure, not another county. Three ways of building that baseline are offered (pick one with the buttons above); whichever is active, counties averaging fewer than 5 arrests/week under that method's own baseline show as “not enough data for a trend” rather than a percentage -- a county averaging 1/week and seeing 3 one week is literally “+200%” but not a meaningful trend.
processing_geography_caveat: This layer shows ICE's own apprehension_city field, aggregated by week. A direct check (on the whole-period total, carried forward unchanged here) found that EVERY one of the 25 highest-count counties has 66-100% of its arrests recorded in a single city that hosts an ICE hold room, processing center, or detention facility -- meaning a spike shown here can be a spike in processing/hold activity, not necessarily a spike in street arrests nearby. Two counties (Del Rio/Val Verde TX, Laredo/Webb TX) read as genuine border-crossing hotspots rather than processing artifacts, since the facility town is itself the crossing point -- the rest cannot be told apart from a processing artifact with this data alone.
entry_format: [week_index, count, flat_baseline_or_null, flat_pct_or_null, guard1_baseline_or_null, guard1_pct_or_null, ewma_baseline_or_null, ewma_pct_or_null]
